func_hero_subtitle: The Bruut platform is a versatile tool carrier. Discover all modules and attachments you can add for specific tasks in the field, greenhouse, or yard.
func_1_desc: Front-mounted or mid-mounted between the front and rear wheels. Usable as a grader for leveling terrain, for pushing feed and grass back in the stable, or for cleaning silos.
func_2_desc: Trencher for digging wet buffer strips and drainage ditches, so standing water is carried off the field efficiently.
func_3_desc: Compact cultivator for soil cultivation in vegetable gardens and light plots.
func_4_desc: Hoeing unit with single-axis (left/right) guidance that stays tightly between the rows, for example in maize, so weeds are cut close to the crop without damaging it.
func_5_desc: Mechanical weed control using rotating fingers in light soil.
func_6_desc: Front-mounted boom with conventional high-pressure nozzles that atomise the liquid into a fine mist. Each nozzle is switched individually, so only the detected weed is treated while the fine droplets fully cover the leaf surface. Based on the 'Open Weed Locator' project and ideal for contact herbicides and crop protection products.
func_7_desc: Boom with individually controlled injectors that fire single coarse droplets on demand at low pressure. Every droplet is placed straight onto the weed, which practically eliminates drift and cuts chemical usage to a fraction of a conventional spray pass.
func_8_desc: Two-axis system with CNC movement (left/right and up/down) carrying a drill that grinds individual weeds out of the sward. Developed for tap-rooted weeds such as broad-leaved dock, fully chemical-free.
func_9_desc: Improving soil structure and air supply in grassland.
func_10_desc: Mowing at various heights, including 'topping' plants above ground level.
func_11_desc: Flexible arm with a brush cutter head or blades for mowing under fences and around obstacles.
func_12_desc: Pumping water from ditches for local irrigation or crop spraying.
func_13_desc: Precise application and spreading of granular fertilizers.
func_14_desc: Spreading lime to improve soil pH levels and structure.
func_15_desc: Seed box for initial crop sowing and for overseeding existing grassland in one pass.
func_16_desc: Front-mounted unit that takes seedlings out of the tray and sets them out at the right spacing.
func_17_desc: Compact seeder that spreads grass seed onto bare patches in the sward, so damaged spots close up again quickly.
func_18_desc: Even distribution of sawdust or bedding material in stables.
func_19_desc: Evenly spreading straw, specially designed for use between vegetable rows.
func_20_desc: Transporting compost within the frame structure and spreading it between the crop rows.
func_21_desc: Additional power supply modules to be installed between the frames.
func_22_desc: Generator or combustion engine mounted between the frame as an auxiliary power source for extra electricity or mechanical power.
func_23_desc: Integrated panels to extend battery life and provide sustainable power during operation.
func_24_desc: Electric motors such as the Ego Power+ or Greenworks units to drive implements that need real power, replacing small petrol engines.
func_25_desc: Large front-mounted brush or electrically driven radial brush for surface cleaning, as an alternative to the front push blade.
func_26_desc: Front or rear-mounted seat, with the option to widen the frame tubes at the sides.
func_27_desc: Motorized wheelbarrow-style bin for transporting and dumping loose materials, also usable as a carrying aid or mini dumper.
func_28_desc: Rear-mounted hitch for pulling trailers and other rolling equipment.
func_29_desc: Ballast weights to improve traction and vehicle balance for heavy tasks.
func_30_desc: External hydraulic power source for applications where hydraulics are a better option than electricity.
func_31_desc: Standard lifting system for attaching various agricultural implements.
func_32_desc: Protective enclosure or housing for the operator.
func_33_desc: Measuring grass and crop height and health to create task maps for nitrogen or phosphate.
func_34_desc: Measuring and mapping soil density at specific data points.
func_35_desc: Near-infrared sensor that measures the NDVI of the crop while driving. From the difference between reflected red and near-infrared light the robot reads biomass, ground cover and crop vitality, and builds live task maps for variable-rate fertilisation. Because the sensor moves close over the crop instead of looking down from a satellite, the readings stay reliable under cloud cover and also register small spots and gaps.
func_36_desc: The robot works together with a drone as a mobile base station. The drone flies out from the platform, maps the plot from above and passes its imagery straight to the robot, which converts it into a driving and treatment plan. The drone charges and swaps batteries on the robot, so the pair can keep scouting and working alternately for a full day without anyone coming out to the field.
func_37_desc: Several Bruut units work the same field as one swarm. The job is split into sections, the robots divide the passes among themselves and keep each other informed of position, progress and battery state, so they never overlap or cross. Capacity scales simply with the number of units instead of with machine size, work continues when one unit drops out, and the light platforms keep soil compaction low.
func_38_desc: Dosing unit for liquid fertiliser, built for RENURE: mineral nitrogen recovered from animal manure, which the EU allows as a replacement for fossil fertiliser. This closes the nutrient cycle on the farm or in the region and reduces the need for fertiliser whose production uses a lot of natural gas. The robot works from task maps made by the grass meter, NIR sensor or drone and adjusts the rate per square metre. Where the crop lags behind it gets more, and where there is already enough nitrogen nothing is applied. The liquid goes into the sward just above the ground, with no mist or drift, and a light robot can drive when the land is too wet for a tractor with a tank. Every application is logged with its GPS position, which makes fertiliser record-keeping easier.
func_39_desc: Trailer with a pop-up tent that serves as a mobile shed for the robot. The trailer carries the robot by road from field to field, or stays parked at the edge of the plot so the robot can spend the night there, dry and out of sight. From the tent the robot starts its task remotely, so the farmer does not have to drive out and unload it first.
func_40_desc: Fixed charging point at the edge of the field, like the one a robotic lawn mower uses. When the battery runs low, the robot drives to the station by itself, docks, recharges and then carries on from where it left off. Large plots are finished over several rounds without anyone having to fetch the robot or plug it in.
func_41_desc: In Cycly mode the robot stays on one plot for a longer period. Every few days it runs a weeder harrow over the field to remove weeds at the seedling stage, before they can take hold. It uses the weather forecast to pick the dry spells between showers, so it does not smear the soil. In between it recharges at the charging station or in the trailer. Through the cameras the farmer keeps an eye on the crop and the robot remotely, without having to go out to the field.
func_42_desc: When spreading fertiliser or sowing, the robot drives to a supply hopper on the headland once its bin is empty and refills automatically. It then returns to the spot where it stopped and continues the pass. This way a small, light platform can still cover a large plot, with nobody needed on site to top it up.
func_43_desc: The robot as a mobile wildlife deterrent, with a 360-degree camera and solar panels so it can stay out in the field day and night. It moves along with your livestock in the pasture, or drives a set patrol around the plot to keep geese, wild boar or wolves at bay. Using AI it recognises the animals on the camera feed and learns from earlier visits when and where they usually turn up, so it is already there before the damage is done. When wildlife comes into view it scares the animals off with sound and light, and the farmer gets an alert on their phone straight away. Because the robot keeps changing position and varies its deterrent each time, animals get used to it far less quickly than to a fixed bird banger or scarecrow.
func_44_desc: Through a belt or chain drive that turns with the robot's travel, it can power existing mechanically driven implements, such as a small ELHO tedder or rake. The rotating parts of the implement run in step with the driving speed, just like the old ground-driven machines behind a horse or tractor. The implement itself needs no separate motor, electronics or hydraulics, giving simple, robust and often second-hand machines a second life behind an autonomous robot.
